_meta.description: Shell plc reporting segments (Shell Annual Report / Form 20-F FY2024) with deep content for per-business pages. FY2024 adjusted earnings shown where relevant. Note: Shell moved 'wholesale commercial fuels' from Chemicals & Products into Marketing effective 1 Jan 2024.

segments.name: Integrated Gas
segments.realCredit: LNG carrier — photo by Gordon Leggett, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
segments.description: Integrated Gas runs Shell's liquefied natural gas (LNG) business end-to-end — producing natural gas, liquefying it, shipping it, and trading and marketing it worldwide. It also includes gas-to-liquids (GTL), turning natural gas into cleaner-burning fuels, lubricants and chemical feedstocks.

facts.text: Largest single profit driver: $11.4B adjusted earnings in 2024 (~48% of group)
World's largest LNG trader — roughly 17% of global LNG trade
LNG sales ~65.8 Mt; liquefaction volumes ~29.1 Mt in 2024
Operates ~10% of the world's LNG shipping fleet
Targets ~4–5% annual LNG sales growth to 2030

segments.connects: Gas feeds liquefaction and trading; GTL output supplies cleaner fuels and base oils used by Chemicals & Products and Marketing. LNG also underpins Renewables & Energy Solutions' power and trading desks.
segments.challenge: Shell brands gas as the lower-carbon 'transition fuel' and is growing LNG, drawing criticism that this entrenches fossil dependence and methane-leak risk. Earnings swing with global gas prices.

segments.name: Upstream
segments.realCredit: North Sea oil platform — photo by NAC, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
segments.description: Upstream explores for, develops and produces crude oil and natural gas — for transport fuels, energy and petrochemical feedstocks. Shell has focused this on a smaller set of high-value, lower-cost, lower-carbon-intensity positions.

facts.text: $8.4B adjusted earnings in 2024 (~35% of group) — second-largest driver
Produced ~1.5 million barrels of liquids per day in 2024
Plus ~7.7 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day
Concentrated in deepwater: US Gulf of Mexico and Brazil pre-salt
Sold its US Permian shale business to ConocoPhillips ($9.5B, 2021)

flagship: Gulf of Mexico (Perdido, Mars, Vito, Whale)
segments.connects: Upstream crude and gas feed Chemicals & Products refineries and Integrated Gas liquefaction; the fuels ultimately reach customers through Marketing.
segments.challenge: Shell softened earlier pledges to cut oil output ~1–2%/year, instead holding production broadly stable to 2030 — welcomed by investors, criticised by climate advocates. Legacy Nigerian operations face long-running spill litigation.

segments.name: Marketing
segments.realCredit: Shell service station — photo by Hugh Venables, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
segments.description: Marketing sells fuels and services directly to people and businesses — through Shell-branded stations, convenience retail, lubricants, fleet solutions, aviation, marine and EV charging. It is Shell's most consumer-facing, higher-margin downstream business.

facts.text: $3.9B adjusted earnings in 2024 (~16% of group)
~47,000 Shell-branded retail sites across 80+ markets
~33 million customers served daily
World's #1 finished-lubricants supplier for 18+ years (~11.6% share)
Scaling EV charging toward a 200,000 charge-point target by 2030

segments.connects: Marketing is the demand-side outlet for fuels refined by Chemicals & Products and base oils from Integrated Gas — turning the group's molecules into branded, higher-margin sales.
segments.challenge: Shell is rationalising its retail footprint (divesting ~500–1,000 sites) and recalibrating EV ambitions toward fast-charging hubs after slower-than-expected EV demand — read by some as a pullback from electrification.

segments.name: Chemicals & Products
segments.realCredit: Oil refinery — photo by W.carter, Wikimedia Commons (CC0)
segments.description: This segment refines crude oil into fuels and feedstocks and manufactures petrochemicals used in packaging, electronics and more. It houses oil-products trading and is the focus of Shell's 'energy and chemicals parks' transformation.

facts.text: $2.9B adjusted earnings in 2024 (~12% of group)
Earnings fell sharply in 2024 on weak refining & chemicals margins
Converting refineries into integrated energy & chemicals parks
Reduced its refinery portfolio from 14 sites to about 5–6
Shell Polymers Monaca (Pennsylvania) cracker came online in 2022

segments.connects: Refineries process Upstream and third-party crude into fuels sold by Marketing and feedstocks for petrochemicals; trading optimises product flows across the whole group.
segments.challenge: Structural overcapacity and weak margins have pressured chemicals; Shell has reviewed and divested some assets while pivoting parks toward lower-carbon products. Monaca has faced local air-quality scrutiny.

segments.name: Renewables & Energy Solutions
segments.realCredit: Egmond aan Zee offshore wind farm — photo by Supercarwaar, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
segments.description: This segment covers renewable power generation, power and environmental-products trading, hydrogen, electric mobility and electricity supply. It is Shell's main vehicle for the energy transition — pairing nascent low-carbon assets with a large power-trading business.

facts.text: Adjusted loss of ~$0.5B in 2024; trading partly offset asset losses
Holland Hydrogen I: a 200 MW electrolyser, Europe's largest green-H₂ plant
CrossWind JV built the 759 MW Hollandse Kust Noord wind farm
Owns sonnen (home batteries / virtual power plant, Germany)
Trimmed some renewables ambitions under a 'value over volume' strategy

segments.connects: Renewable power and hydrogen support Shell's own decarbonisation (e.g. green H₂ to the Rotterdam park) and supply electrons for Marketing's EV charging; trading integrates with the other segments' optimisation.
segments.challenge: The segment is persistently loss-making and Shell has retreated from several clean-power commitments — exiting some power-retail markets, scaling back offshore wind, and dropping a 2035 interim carbon-intensity target — drawing criticism that it is deprioritising the transition.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.description: Corporate covers Shell's holding-company functions, group financing and treasury, self-insurance, and central headquarters costs not allocated to the operating segments. It is a cost centre that funds and underwrites the rest of the group.

facts.text: Adjusted-earnings drag of ~$2.0B in 2024 (interest, tax, central costs)
Returned ~$8.7B in dividends to shareholders in 2024
Plus ~$14.1B in share buybacks in 2024
Houses group treasury, financing and self-insurance
Bears costs of the 2022 consolidation into a single UK plc

segments.connects: Corporate allocates capital across all five operating segments, manages the balance sheet, and channels their cash flows into dividends and buybacks.
segments.challenge: Capital allocation is the central debate: large buybacks and shareholder returns please investors but are criticised by climate advocates as money that could fund the transition faster.
